Title: Q: When to replace Action Mod's during vote? L. Scott?

Messages.Author: Robert Goudie
Messages.Body:
Hi all,

I have seen L. Scott Johnson's rules reference and in some related posts
he states (if I'm not mistaken) that during a vote no cards are
replaced. This seems to include cards such as bewitching oration. Is
that correct??? The V:tes rulebook says explicitly that vote cards used
for extra votes are not replaced but in context it is obviously talking
only about Political Action cards. Can someone please clarify?

Also, with the new DC rules, do you replace your initial Political
Action card immediately like you used to or do you have to wait until
the end of your turn on that too? What about cards like Bewitching
Oration? Do you replace those at the end of your turn also? Hmmm???

Robert

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
Robert Goudie <robert...@studio.disney.com> writes:
>I have seen L. Scott Johnson's rules reference and in some related posts
>he states (if I'm not mistaken) that during a vote no cards are
>replaced. This seems to include cards such as bewitching oration. Is
>that correct??? The V:tes rulebook says explicitly that vote cards used
>for extra votes are not replaced but in context it is obviously talking
>only about Political Action cards. Can someone please clarify?

"No cards" is correct. This includes ActMod/React cards.
The new rulebook's text is unclear on its scope, to be sure, so I had
Tom clarify the point a while back:

From: aa...@cats.ucsc.edu (Thomas R Wylie)
Newsgroups: rec.games.trading-cards.jyhad
Subject: Re: [VtES][PR] Full Rulebook, 1 of 2
Date: 30 Sep 1995 01:42:50 GMT
Message-ID: <44i7aq$8...@darkstar.UCSC.EDU>

L. Scott Johnson <sjoh...@math.scarolina.edu> wrote:
>>Any Methuselah can burn extra political cards for extra votes. Each burned
>>political card is worth one vote. If you burn an extra political card,
>>ignore the effects printed on the card and throw it into your ash heap.
>>You can't, however, draw new cards until the political action is finished.
>
>This unfortunate wording makes it easy to miss the fact that Action
>Modifiers and Reaction cards cannot be replaced.

Hm, probably so.

>(You do mean that *no* cards can be replaced, right? Not just that PAs
>burned for votes may not be replaced?)

Right.

>Also, with the new DC rules, do you replace your initial Political
>Action card immediately like you used to or do you have to wait until
>the end of your turn on that too? What about cards like Bewitching
>Oration? Do you replace those at the end of your turn also? Hmmm???

You still replace the card used to take the action immediately, as always.
And only PAs burned for votes are governed by the new DCI rule. Other
vote-modifying cards (ActMods and Reactions) are replaced at the end of the
action, as normal.
